## bambaganaCI {#bambaganaci}

**Authors:** Silas Bambil and Yasmeen Babagana.

An R package for constructing confidence intervals for a population mean. It implements percentile, basic, normal, and bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap intervals, together with the classical Student's t interval. A comparison function reports interval endpoints and widths across methods using the same data.

The package includes input checks, reproducible resampling methods, and automated tests. The source code is publicly available on [GitHub](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI). Version 0.1.1 is not currently available on CRAN.
:::

### Supported confidence intervals

| Method | Function or argument | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Percentile bootstrap | `method = "percentile"` | Uses empirical quantiles of resampled means |
| Basic bootstrap | `method = "basic"` | Reflects bootstrap quantiles about the sample mean |
| Normal bootstrap | `method = "normal"` | Uses a bootstrap standard error and estimated bias correction |
| BCa bootstrap | `method = "bca"` | Adjusts bootstrap endpoints for bias and acceleration |
| Classical Student's t | `mean_t_ci()` | Uses the t distribution and sample standard error |

### Installation from GitHub

Install the development tool `remotes` if needed, then install `bambaganaCI` directly from its public GitHub repository.

```{.r}
install.packages("remotes")  # Run once if needed
remotes::install_github("sdbambil1/bambaganaCI")
library(bambaganaCI)
```

[Source code and documentation](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI) · [Version 0.1.1 release](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI/releases/tag/v0.1.1)

### R examples

The examples below use the publicly available package source. The package is not currently distributed through CRAN.

**Example 1. Bootstrap confidence interval for a mean**

```{.r}
library(bambaganaCI)

set.seed(1998)
x <- rnorm(30, mean = 2, sd = 1)

result <- bootstrap_mean_ci(
  x, B = 2000, conf = 0.95,
  method = "percentile"
)

print(result)
confint(result)
```

The function returns the sample mean, interval endpoints, bootstrap standard error, and resampled means.

**Example 2. Compare interval construction methods**

```{.r}
set.seed(1998)
x <- rexp(30)

comparison <- compare_mean_ci(
  x, B = 2000, conf = 0.95,
  methods = c("percentile", "basic",
              "normal", "bca", "t")
)

print(comparison)
```

The resulting table includes the mean estimate, lower and upper confidence limits, and interval width for each method. Bootstrap methods within a single comparison share resamples.

**Example 3. Classical t interval**

```{.r}
result_t <- mean_t_ci(x, conf = 0.95)
print(result_t)
confint(result_t)
```

### Assumptions and limitations

Bootstrap intervals here assume independent, identically distributed observations and target the ordinary population mean. The classical t interval has exact coverage under independent normal sampling with positive common variance. Coverage can differ from the nominal level for skewed, heavy-tailed, or contaminated populations, particularly with small samples. The package does not automatically handle clusters, serial dependence, survey weights, or missing observations. Comparisons illustrate differences between interval methods; they do not establish that one method is universally preferable.

## shiftadapt {#shiftadapt}

An R package under development for updating logistic prediction models under distribution shift. It implements candidate updating policies, validation-based selection, and evaluation on independent test data.
:::

### Four updating strategies

| Strategy | What it does |
|---|---|
| Retain | Uses the original model without updating |
| Intercept-only recalibration | Updates the baseline risk |
| Intercept-and-slope recalibration | Updates the intercept and the scale of the original linear predictor |
| Full logistic refit | Re-estimates the model coefficients |

### A separated evaluation workflow

::: {.workflow}
::: {}
<span class="eyebrow">01 · Adaptation data</span>

### Fit the updates

Estimate the candidate updating strategies.
:::
::: {}
<span class="eyebrow">02 · Validation data</span>

### Select a strategy

Compare candidates using validation log loss.
:::
::: {}
<span class="eyebrow">03 · Test data</span>

### Evaluate performance

Assess the selected strategy on untouched observations.
:::
:::

<details class="methods"><summary>Selection rules & performance measures</summary>

The package supports minimum validation log loss and a paired one-standard-error rule. The latter favors a simpler strategy whose validation performance is within one paired standard error of the minimum.

Evaluation includes log loss, Brier score, ROC-AUC, and calibration diagnostics.

</details>

## Ridge regression package {#ridge-package}

<div class="status-line"><span class="badge planned">Planned project</span><span>R package · Regularized regression</span></div>

A planned R package for ridge regression, with an emphasis on coefficient shrinkage, penalty selection through cross-validation, and out-of-sample prediction assessment. The package is at the planning stage; no completed implementation or release is claimed.
